details: On April 17, reports indicated Iran had reopened the Strait of Hormuz, leading to a surge in Bitcoin. However, subsequent reports on April 18 suggest that Iran has either again closed the Strait until the US lifts the blockade or that firms are seeking clarification amid a US military blockade. This shift creates uncertainty and a risk-off sentiment in financial markets.
sourceName: Multiple (Al Jazeera, The Guardian, MarketForces Africa, The Motley Fool, KuCoin)
title: Iran Strait of Hormuz: Reopening Followed by Conflicting Reports and Blockade Concerns

details: Iran has reportedly demanded that ships pay tolls for accessing the Strait of Hormuz in cryptocurrency. This demand comes amidst a U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports and new U.S. sanctions, highlighting crypto's role in sanctions evasion and illicit financing, which carries regulatory risks.
title: Iran Demands Crypto for Hormuz Tolls Amid US Blockade

details: The Financial Stability Board (FSB) has issued a warning about a potential severe financial crisis, a "triple whammy" combining tighter funding, war-driven market volatility, and deepening issues in non-bank finance. This could significantly impact global financial stability and lead to a risk-off environment for crypto.
title: FSB Warns of "Triple Whammy" Global Financial Crisis
